headline: Approved taking action on an in-vessel composting proposal to be submitted to the Mayor's Office, 3 yeas, 1 absent.
summary: Commissioners heard from a regional official about tire recycling, fire extinguisher disposal, and food waste plans. They also discussed textile swaps and a possible grant for a promotional video.
decisions: Approved taking action on the in-vessel composting proposal, 3 yeas, 1 absent.

decision_titles: In-vessel composting proposal for the Mayor's Office
plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Solid Waste & Recycling Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
7:00 PM, August 12, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER   
 Chairman Kosowsky called the meeting to order at at 7:14 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE/ROLL CALL   
 Present: Alice Kosowsky, chair; Theresa Allgood; Shenira Billups. 
Absent: Eben Pariser. 
Also Present: P.J. Deak; Alison DeMaio; Joe DeRisi, Recycling Coordinator; Robert Velez, 
clerk; Kate Wimsatt, Regional Solid Waste & Recycling Specialist of the South Central 
Regional Council of Governments. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 
 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE: As Submitted   
 
 
  1. Phone call from Rose Lion regarding opportunities to reach out to the Legislative 
Council.  
  
• Chairman Kosowsky spoke about a phone call received from Rose Lion, to 
communicate with the Legislatice Council. 
• She spoke about a second piece of correspondence regarding the 5 Steps to 
Reducing Waste Management Costs. Chairman Kosowsky read from the 
aforementioned article.  
• Alice Kosowsky called for a motion to change the agenda and speak about old 
business, item 1 next. 
o The motion was approved 3yeas, 1 absent 
 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 There was no executive session. 
7. NEW BUSINESS
1. Visit from Kate Wimsatt, SCRCOG Solid Waste & Recycling official. Ms. Wimsatt will address 
the Commission on SCRCOG plans and projects: EPR for tires, Fire Extinguisher disposal, and 
the creation & management of a new category of resource recovery, Food Waste. She will 
highlight the role of Town commissions and other groups in facilitating community 
participation in new solid waste management practices.   
  
• Chairman Kosowsky asked Kate Wimsatt to speak on a number of topics in an 
effort to mobilize the commission and provide insight on a number of topics. 
• Ms. Wimsatt spoke to the commission about engagement between the town 
and SCRCOG. 
• She also spoke about SCRCOG's proposal on applying to a proposal on 
behalf of Hamden and SCRCOG to turn waste into energy. 
• She mentioned there are grant opportunities for community gardens. 
 
8. OLD BUSINESS   
 
 
  1. Update on Proposal for In-Vessel Composting, to be submitted to the Mayor’s Office. 
Commissioner Eben Pariser to conduct this section.   
  
• Chairman Kosowsky asked Joe DeRisi if he has spoken with the Mayor.  
o He responded that his meeting with the Mayor is tomorrow morning 
from the date of this meeting. 
• Chairman Kosowsky spoke about commissioner Pariser providing suggestions 
to Mayor Adam Sendroff for consideration. 
• Guest Speaker Kate Wimsatt commented that the South Central Regional 
Council of Governments would be interested in assisting where it could. 
 
  2. Components of the Proposal after a group brainstorm in the rain.  
  
• Chairman Kosowsky asked Joe to speak about continuous flow regarding 
invesseled containers at the transfer station. She also said the labor 
component would be minimal and not interfere with operations. 
• The last component to the proposal is that the commission apply for a grant to 
increase education on composting. She mentioned there are crowd sourcing 
grants and mentioned Cheshire received one in 2025; she added the 
commission should apply for grants such as these. 
•  
 
  3. Reactions & suggestions.  
  
• The commission showed interest in moving forward on the proposal. 
 
  4. Vote to approve or disapprove proposal plan.
• Chairman Kosowsky called for a vote to approve or disapprove of these 
actions. 
o The commission voted 3 yeas and 1 absent to approve taking action 
on the proposal. 
 
  5. Update on Textile Recycling through Swaps & Donation. Chairperson Kosowsky to 
lead the discussion regarding the 4 swaps planned for 2026, role clarification for 
activities before, during & after the swaps. Statistics.    
  
• Chairman Kosowsky gave an update on textiles through Swaps & Donations 
and said the commission has been approved by the town for the commission 
to be the official host. 
o She commented that Brooksvale is all set and she has spoken with the 
director at the Keefe Center. 
o She has had less success reaching the Knights of Columbus lodge. 
o Chairman Kosowsky offered to send the commissioner she had been 
trying to reach. 
o Joe DeRisi mentioned the town had collected 4,100 tons of collected 
textiles for recycling which the town is able to receive a small sum of 
money for, about $120.00 per ton.  
 
  6. Bringing the Community into Solid Waste Management Change. Should we apply for 
the free video creation that Commissioners Allgood & Billups have investigated? 
Discussion about topic, timing. Intercommission communication. Vote.   
  
• Chairman Kosowsky mentioned that Kate Wimsatt has given the commission 
ideas for education programs. 
o She also mentioned she would like to speak to the town about writing 
the grant and ask if the commission could write the grant or if it should 
be someone else. 
o Commissioner Allgood spoke about someone who would be willing to 
generate a promotional video. 
 
9. ADJOURNMENT   
 
• Chairman Kosowsky called for the meeting to adjourn at 8:20 PM. 
o Commissioner Allgood seconded the motion. 
o The motion passed 3 yeas, 1 absent.
